quotes.text: People think performing is the hard part. The hard part is the hour after. You come off stage and your entire body is convinced you are still the most important person on earth and then you're standing in a parking structure looking for a shuttle. That is a hard landing, my friend.
quotes.speaker: Bill Hicks
quotes.context: Post-show Q&A, Laff Stop, Austin, Texas, recorded for the archive later released as Dangerous: Live at the Laff Stop, 1990
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Hicks's habit of undercutting his own grandiosity and his eye for the mundane humiliation inside showbiz are well-established. The giveaway is 'my friend' as a closer — Hicks addressed his audience more as 'people' or 'folks' and rarely used that direct intimate tag.

quotes.text: Here's what Vegas is: it's the only city where you can lose three grand, eat a steak the size of your face at two in the morning, and still feel like you won something. That's engineering. Somebody sat down and engineered that feeling. I respect it. I hate it. I respect it.

quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Kinison's love-hate relationship with excess and his signature doubling-back rhetorical structure ('I respect it. I hate it.') fit perfectly.
